title: Ghost Type
description: Christina Rossetti’s “Who Has Seen the Wind?” set huge as a justified block of heavy type. Pull any word out and place it anywhere on the page, or type your own words and drag them in; everything you move trails outlined ghosts that ripple like cloth, and the lines re-justify around the gaps. Drop a word back on its gap and it flies home.
intent: Type as cloth you can rearrange: heavy words lift out of a justified block, trail computed outline ghosts while they move and stay wherever you set them down, so the poem becomes a page you compose.

sources.name: A Drift by Robert Aperios (Codrops, 2026)
sources.what: The technique of cached glyph canvases bent by one-pixel slices (0.72 sin + 0.28 cos), a five-ghost outline stack with pow(1 - age/5, 1.35) opacity and a cycling phase; re-derived, no files copied (the repo has no licence).

sources.name: Christina Rossetti, “Who Has Seen the Wind?” (Sing-Song, 1872)
